title: Why Bad Behavior Becomes a Pattern in a Relationship
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article explains how unspoken relationship rules quietly get rewritten through repeated, unaddressed behavior. When someone crosses a line and the other person says nothing, the violator is implicitly free to repeat it, and after enough repetitions without pushback, the exception effectively becomes a new rule governing the relationship. The author notes several understandable reasons people avoid confronting these violations in the moment, including conflict aversion and power imbalances, but warns that the longer the pattern goes unaddressed, the harder it becomes to reverse. The piece frames relationship rules as something negotiated continuously through daily actions rather than settled once at the outset. It closes by urging readers to be selective about which battles to fight, but to address genuine rule violations early, before they harden into fixtures of the relationship.
points: Unspoken rules govern most of what happens in a relationship, from candor to response times
Letting a rule violation pass without discussion implicitly grants permission to repeat it
Repeated unaddressed violations eventually harden into new, unspoken rules
Relationship rules are negotiated continuously, not settled once, through the actions each party accepts
quotes: These rules (how candid we can be, when we can interrupt, etc.) allow the parties to interact harmoniously and productively, and without unnecessary conflict.
We say nothing, even though we are bothered by the rule violation.
Naturally, this means the other party is free to repeat the behavior without consequence.
If and when the other party engages in the inappropriate or distasteful behavior a few more times without any pushback, resistance, or confrontation, then a new rule exists in the relationship.
The key to remember is this: The rules in any relationship are negotiated and affirmed every day through the actions each party accepts.
Pick your battles wisely, but be sure to address rule violations before they spin out of control and create a pattern that is nearly impossible to break.
